acceptance_tests.evidence: Measured in real Chromium at 720x450 CSS px, which is exactly what 200% zoom produces from a 1440x900 window: documentElement.scrollWidth 720 == clientWidth 720, so no horizontal overflow; the primary action button is visible with offsetParent set and a computed 14px font. Token-side, --font-size-base is 100% (not px) so rem layout scales, --text-body is 14px and --text-label 12px, and .app-main does not use overflow:hidden. A test that incorrectly demanded 100vh be removed was corrected before implementing — browser zoom does not change CSS px, so 100vh does not clip at 200%, and switching it to min-height would move scroll containment to the document, the behaviour redesign this task forbids.

Driven by real Tab presses so :focus-visible genuinely matches (element.focus() does not trigger it in Chromium — the first sweep read the text colour at 15.53:1 and was measuring the wrong thing). Computed outlineColor rgb(107,44,23) = --focus #6b2c17, outlineWidth 3px, outlineStyle solid, against the composited panel rgba(255,253,249,0.96): contrast 10.35:1, up from 1.42:1 before this task. The rule covers button, a, input, select and textarea. A unit test also computes the old rgba value and asserts it really was below 3:1, so the regression cannot silently return.

Real-browser emulation, not a text assertion: with reducedMotion 'no-preference' the computed animationName on .page-loading/.gallery-skeleton is 'osteo-shimmer'; with 'reduce' it becomes 'none' and animationDuration '0s'. Transitions and scroll-behavior are neutralised too, and .card:hover transform is removed. Before this task the stylesheet contained no prefers-reduced-motion block at all.

The three class accents measure grayscale 34 / 33 / 34 — interchangeable by luminance, which is recorded deliberately and is precisely why step 04's text+shape pairing is mandatory rather than optional. The distinction is therefore carried by two channels that survive grayscale: the chip renders the literal identifier (verified in-browser as exactly ['NON_TUMOR','VIABLE_TUMOR','NECROSIS']) and the markers are three distinct shapes (border-radius 50% / 0px / polygon clip-path), confirmed distinct in a live DOM query. The accents were NOT repainted — a rebrand would exceed this task's brief. A test asserts no fourth class accent can be added, keeping mixed/uncertain/deferred as review states rather than learned classes.

Behaviour did not change. 89/89 frontend tests pass (61 pre-existing + 28 new), and the full 17/17 Playwright journey — ACCEPT, CORRECT, DEFER, export provenance, attribution honesty — passes against a live backend. Zero component files were modified. On the rendered workbench the before/after screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 were visually indistinguishable on inspection — but NO PIXEL DIFF WAS COMPUTED, so 'identical' is an observation, not a measurement. One intended visual change exists and was NOT covered by those screenshots: .attrib-panel (the G7 attribution panel, not visible in the gallery state) had a stale cool-gray fallback var(--border, #d8dee4) and now renders the earth-tone --border #ddd5cc. That change is recorded as a fix, not verified here by screenshot.

FOUND IN MY OWN TEST — I first asserted height:100vh must be removed. That reasoning was wrong: browser zoom does not change CSS px, so it does not clip at 200%, and switching to min-height would move scroll containment from the inner pane to the document. Corrected before implementation; .app was left untouched.

FOUND IN MY OWN TEST — four assertions were wrong (five failing tests): a token filter matching --text-body/--text-label as colours, a focus regex anchored at ':focus-visible' that dropped the leading 'button', a missing class-name to token-suffix map, and a label matcher expecting 'NON TUMOR' when the chip renders the literal 'NON_TUMOR'. All corrected, none weakened.

FOUND IN MY OWN SWEEP — element.focus() does not trigger :focus-visible in Chromium, so the first browser sweep measured the text colour (15.53:1) and would have passed while testing the wrong property. Now driven by real Tab presses.

TOOLING LIMITATION DISCOVERED — Vite's ?raw, ?inline and import.meta.glob all return a ZERO-LENGTH string for CSS under this project's css:false vitest setting, and an ambient declare-module block is illegal inside a module file. A filesystem read is therefore the only way to assert real stylesheet content here, behind two @ts-expect-error directives (not @ts-ignore) that fail the build if @types/node is ever added. Installing a type package or widening tsconfig types are both outside this task's authorisation.

NOT ADDRESSED, DISCLOSED — neither --border (1.43:1 on --surface) nor --border-strong (1.80:1) meets the 3:1 non-text floor. They render as decorative dividers and restyling them would be a visual redesign, but any future control relying on a border alone to convey state would fail WCAG 1.4.11. Not claimed as passing.
NOT ADDRESSED, DISCLOSED — sub-12px sizes (10px, 11px) still exist in the professional layer. The contract sets 12px as a target; restyling them was outside this brief.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN EVIDENCE — I wrote that before/after screenshots were 'pixel-identical'. I never computed a pixel diff; they were visually indistinguishable on inspection. Worse, the claim was false as a general statement: .attrib-panel carried var(--border, #d8dee4), a stale cool-gray fallback, and now renders #ddd5cc. The gallery screenshots simply never showed that panel. Corrected in acceptance_tests, ui_browser_observations and limitations.
